newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria raises penalty for gas flaring.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria raises penalty for gas flaring.

text.p: Nigeria has increased the penalty for gas flaring by oil companies to 50 kobo (some 0.625 cents) from two kobo (0.025 cents) for every 1,000 standard cubic feet of gas, oil minister Dan Etete said on Tuesday.

"Currently, some 75 percent of gas produced, equivalent to 300,000 barrels per day of crude oil, is flared," Etete told an oil industry conference in Lagos. "This causes a lot of concern to the government".
To stem the tide of gas flaring, which helps in the extraction of crude oil, the government decided to raise the penalty to encourage firms to gather the gas for uses other than flaring, Etete said.
The conference heard on Monday that oil companies operating in Nigeria would virtually stop all gas flaring by the year 2008 because of a series of gas development projects being undertaken.
Etete said Nigeria's total proven gas reserves are between 150 and 300 trillion cubic feet.
Only 25 percent of Nigeria's gas is utilised at the moment, with the rest being flared.

Among the projects is a $4 billion plan involving major oil companies and Nigeria to build a liquefied natural gas plant that will export 1.082 billion standard cubic feet of gas daily to Europe from 1999.
"This conference (of petroleum explorationists) should evolve cost-effective exploitation strategies for natural gas that would drastically reduce the producer cost," Etete said.
Oil firms say the government must offer incentives to encourage commercial investments in gas utilisation.

A communiqu issued at the end of the conference said the government should set up a joint consultative council on gas development and utilisation consisting of representatives of the producers, third party users, end users and the government.
The council will address issues of demand, pricing and infrastructure for gas.

"Current gas pricing arrangements are haphazard in formulation and implementation and do not meet the combined objectives of encouraging new investments in gas utilisation projects," the communiqu said.
